title: Shoot and Fruit borer on Brinjal

Header: Shoot and Fruit borer on Brinjal
Leucinodes orbonalis In Sinhala-Karati saha gedi vidina panuwa; In Tamil-“Kaththari kai thandu thulaippan”

Prevention: Information on pest history in the area
Establish a 2 m high net barrier or physical barrier using locally available materials (Dried banana leaves, coconut leaves etc.) around the field
Use maize as a barrier crop around brinjal fields (should establish 15 days before transplanting of brinjal)
Do a crop rotation with pulses
Plough the field to expose pupae to sunlight to kill them
Strictly follow the recommended fertilizer practices
Do mixed cropping (e.g. with maize, pulses)
Conserve natural vegetation around the crop to increase population of natural enemies ( Trathala flavo-orbitalis etc.)
Monitoring: Look for withered young shoots and wilted leaves, especially after 1 month of planting.
Observe small holes below the calyx of fruits
Presence of frass and larva inside the damaged shoots and pods
Establish light traps (electric or kerosene- hurricane lamps) to monitor adult moth population
Delay the application of chemicals until the damage exceeds 5% level to increase natural enemies population
Direct Control: Hand pick and destroy infected shoots and fruits
Spray neem seed water extract (30 g of neem seed kernel powder in 1
Separate damaged pods at harvest and deep bury (3 ft) or destroy them to kill larvae
Use kerosinized water trays with light traps to kill adult moths
Restrictions: III (slightly hazardous); Contact insecticide; Disrupt acetylcholine neurotransmission; PHI 7days
II (moderately hazardous); Pyrethroid, Contact and stomach action; Highly toxic to fish and aquatic organisms, must be used with extreme caution around water.
Do not contaminate surface water or ditches; PHI 7 days
WHO U (Unlikely to present acute hazard in normal use); Synthetic diamide pesticide; Specific for
Lepidopterans few non target effects; Stomach and contact insecticide; act on muscular functions of insects; PHI 7 days
